title: fix: keep unknown usage out of paid breakdowns
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16440

- Counts only explicit `pack` rows in Paid request/Pollen totals and model breakdowns, matching the existing chart classification.
- Keeps unknown/null rows in overall aggregates without labeling them Paid or Quest.
- Adds one regression for mixed unknown/null/pack/tier usage through the real hook.
- Verified: 15 focused tests, scoped Biome and actual rendered-badge controls; the regression fails on baseline.

Full Enter build/typecheck remain blocked by missing cached dependencies with identical baseline diagnostics. The Cloudflare suite was not run because its required secret setup was unavailable.

gist.headline: Paid means pack, actually
gist.blurb: The activity page gets a tidier ledger: only requests explicitly marked as pack usage count as Paid. Unknown usage still counts toward the overall total, without being assigned a category it never had.
gist.summary: Enter’s activity breakdown counts only explicit `pack` rows in Paid request and Pollen totals and per-model breakdowns, matching the chart while retaining unknown and null rows in overall aggregates.
gist.impact: Users get Paid totals that reflect identified pack usage; unknown and null usage still contributes to overall totals without appearing as Paid or Quest.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Enter’s usage dashboard as a cozy garden ledger: labeled pack tokens go into a Paid basket, while unmarked tokens remain in an overall-total basket. Polli, wearing tiny accountant glasses, sorts the tokens; a small code-plant and lime-green screen tie the scene to the activity UI.
